score_rationale: SBA loan recipients are a proven high-value B2B prospect segment (banks, fintechs, and B2B SaaS all pay for this). SBA publishes FOIA data at data.sba.gov with no auth barrier. The COVID-era PPP data awareness has faded; the ongoing 7(a) and 504 loan data is far less well-known and not productized as an affordable flat file. Score 7 not 8 because the data is available annually (not monthly), and the buyer's primary use case (prospecting) faces mild competition from Dun & Bradstreet and Experian Business.
summary: A cleaned CSV of all approved SBA 7(a) and 504 small business loans sourced from the SBA FOIA data portal (data.sba.gov) — fully public and downloadable without authentication. Each record includes the borrower business name, city, state, ZIP, NAICS code, jobs reported, loan amount approved, SBA-guaranteed amount, lender name, lender city and state, loan program type (7a or 504), and approval date. Dun & Bradstreet, Experian Business, and ZoomInfo all resell versions of SBA loan recipient data at $200–$2,000+ per export. A one-time $49 CSV targets non-SBA lenders identifying active loan recipients as upsell prospects, B2B SaaS vendors finding recently-capitalized small businesses at the moment of growth investment, and business brokers/acquisition advisers tracking SBA-financed companies — all segments currently paying subscription rates for the same DOL public data.

audience.who: Non-SBA commercial lenders and community banks identifying businesses that received SBA 7(a) or 504 loans in the past 24 months as prospects for working capital lines, equipment financing, and treasury management services — SBA loan recipients are by definition creditworthy and growth-oriented; fintech lenders (Kabbage, OnDeck, Funding Circle) who want to identify SBA-approved borrowers as warm leads for supplemental capital products; B2B SaaS vendors (payroll, HR, accounting, ERP) who target businesses at the growth stage when they just received SBA capital — the most actionable buying signal for business software; business brokers and M&A advisers tracking SBA 504 loan recipients (who financed real estate or equipment) as potential acquisition targets or seller referrals; SBA-focused CPAs and business consultants who want a list of every recent SBA loan recipient in their state as cold-outreach prospects for year-one compliance and tax planning engagements.

data_wanted: SBA 7(a) and 504 FOIA loan data — downloadable as Excel/CSV files from https://data.sba.gov/dataset/7-a-504-foia. SBA publishes separate files for 7(a) loans (general small business) and 504 loans (commercial real estate and large equipment). Most recent: FY2024 full-year file and FY2025 year-to-date file. Key fields per approved loan: BorrName (business name), BorrStreet, BorrCity, BorrState, BorrZip, BorrCounty, BusinessType (corporation, LLC, sole proprietor, partnership), FranchiseName, ProjectCounty, ProjectState, SBADistrictOffice, CongressionalDistrict, BusinessAge (existing/new/change-of-ownership), LoanStatus (disbursed in full, cancelled, paid in full, charged off), ApprovalDate, ApprovalFiscalYear, GrossApproval (total approved loan amount), SBAGuaranteedApproval (SBA portion), Term (months), LenderName, LenderCity, LenderState, NAICS code (6-digit), NaicsDescription, JobsSupported, SubPgmCode (program subtype). Scope to approved disbursed loans from FY2022–FY2025 (~300,000–400,000 records). Combine both 7(a) and 504 datasets.

evidence.source: SBA FOIA Data — data.sba.gov publishes complete 7(a) and 504 loan approval data as downloadable CSV/Excel files for all fiscal years, no authentication required
evidence.quote: SBA 7(a) and 504 Loan Data: FOIA disclosure data for all SBA 7(a) and 504 loan approvals by fiscal year. Includes borrower name, city, state, NAICS code, lender, loan amount, and guarantee amount. Downloadable as Excel files.

evidence.source: Dun & Bradstreet Small Business Solutions — D&B resells SBA loan recipient data as part of its small business prospecting lists, with custom exports starting at $500+ for filtered lists of recent SBA borrowers by state and industry
evidence.quote: D&B Small Business Solutions provides targeted prospect lists of US small businesses, including SBA loan recipients, new business formations, and growth-stage companies. Custom list pricing from $500 for 1,000 contacts.

evidence.source: SBA Annual Report FY2024 — confirms ~100,000 7(a) loans approved per year at an average of $500K+, establishing the scale and commercial significance of the borrower population
evidence.quote: In FY2024, SBA approved approximately 70,000 7(a) loans totaling $31.1 billion and 11,000 504 loans totaling $10.4 billion, supporting small business growth across all 50 states and US territories.

evidence.source: Nav.com — SMB financial platform notes that SBA loan recipients are among the most-targeted segments for follow-on financial services, confirming the commercial prospecting value of identifying recent SBA borrowers
evidence.quote: SBA loan recipients represent the most creditworthy and growth-oriented segment of small businesses. Banks, lenders, and financial service providers actively target SBA borrowers for cross-sell and upsell opportunities.

willingness_to_pay.signal: The core arbitrage: D&B and Experian charge $500–$2,000 for filtered exports of SBA loan recipients while SBA publishes the underlying data free on data.sba.gov. The buyer gets identical data at 1/40th the price. B2B SaaS vendors targeting growth-stage small businesses are the highest-conviction buyer: a $49 CSV of 80,000+ companies that just received SBA capital in the past year is worth the cost of one qualified demo call. Non-SBA lenders are the second tier: identifying $31 billion in annual SBA-approved borrowers as candidates for supplemental credit products is a standard bank prospecting activity. The absence of a cheap, downloadable, clean version of this data at the flat-file price point creates a clear opening.

first_sale_path.channel: Gumroad one-time download + LinkedIn posts targeting commercial bankers, SBA lenders, B2B SaaS SDRs/BDRs, and fintech growth teams + r/smallbusiness, r/Entrepreneur, and r/banking contextual posts + direct LinkedIn outreach to business brokers, SBA-focused CPAs, and community bank business development officers
first_sale_path.angle: Title: 'SBA 7(a) & 504 Loan Recipients FY2022–2025 — 300,000+ Approved Borrowers, NAICS, Lender & Amount (CSV)'. Key selling points: (1) Every business approved for an SBA 7(a) or 504 loan in the last 3 years — business name, city, state, NAICS, loan amount, SBA guarantee, lender, and jobs supported, (2) Direct from SBA FOIA data — the same public records D&B and Experian mark up by 40×, (3) Filter by state, NAICS, or loan size — find every manufacturer in Ohio that received $500K+ in SBA capital last year, (4) One-time $49 instant CSV. B2B SaaS angle: 'Build your dream prospect list — every small business that just got SBA capital and is ready to invest in tools. 300,000+ companies. $49 once.' Lender angle: 'Every SBA 7(a) borrower in your market — by state, NAICS, and loan size. Find your next cross-sell opportunity.'
